q: Computing contingency values within relevant establishing operations rather than across the whole session prevents:
choices: A. The background probability from ever reaching zero
B. Dilution of a contingency that operates only situationally
C. The need for any experimental analysis afterward
D. Observers disagreeing about the behavior definitions used

q: The principal analytic cost of combining several putative reinforcers into one test condition is that the result:
choices: A. Overestimates the overall rate of problem behavior
B. Requires an unusually long observation period
C. Does not isolate which reinforcer is necessary
D. Cannot be used to design any treatment

q: Hagopian et al. (2015) reported that reinforcement-based treatment alone was effective for:
choices: A. Subtype 3 cases only, once restraint was blocked
B. No cases of automatically reinforced self-injury
C. Most Subtype 1 cases but no Subtype 2 cases
D. All three subtypes at comparable rates
